title: Jev / System-One Vision
core_thesis: The useful Jev-like property is not merely one-token output; it is encoding rich state once and cheaply evaluating many independently specified semantic questions against the shared representation.

concepts.text: Jev-like systems are direct decision systems over a semantic representation rather than autoregressive generators. Input understanding still costs compute; serial language decoding can disappear.
A causal LLM can approximate Jev-like behavior by prefill plus next-token logits restricted to candidate answers, then stopping. Any Jev latency claim should be compared against this baseline.
A non-generative system may not call input processing 'prefill', but equivalent semantic computation over the input remains necessary.
Prototype: generate N image crops, batch them through SigLIP/CLIP, encode arbitrary text labels once, and compute an N x M similarity matrix with no autoregressive generation.
Batching N crops is parallel execution but not true compute reuse; overlapping pixels are still repeatedly encoded.

Better architecture: encode the full image once into a dense spatial feature map, extract N region embeddings with ROI pooling or learned queries, then score all regions against M dynamic predicates in parallel.
Predicates need not be object labels. Examples include objectness, damage, corrosion, leakage, graspability, danger, abnormality, missing fastener, and temporal identity.
Relevant families include CLIP/SigLIP, DETR, SAM, open-vocabulary detection, ROIAlign, region-language models, and calibrated classifiers.
The target abstraction is one scene representation plus N spatial queries times M semantic predicates, yielding a large direct decision matrix.

roadmap: v1: shared full-image features + ROI queries
